caption:
You don't build automations anymore — you just describe them.

For over a decade, Zapier meant dragging boxes around: trigger here, action there, test it, watch it silently break on step three, dig through a log to find out why. That fiddly chain-building was the whole job.

In July 2026, after an extended beta, Zapier's AI Agents feature hit general availability — and it changes what "automation" even means for a non-technical person. Instead of wiring steps together, you describe the outcome in plain English, and an agent constructs, runs, and maintains the entire multi-step workflow itself. It can branch into different paths depending on what it finds, and recover from errors on its own instead of just stopping.

It's built on top of Zapier's existing catalog of 7,000+ app integrations, so it already talks to your email, calendar, spreadsheets, CRM, and social accounts — this isn't a walled-garden AI chatbot starting from zero. And it's not just an office tool: the same builder works for things like logging package emails into your notes or rolling starred newsletters into one weekly digest.

One honest caveat: giving an agent broad permission to act across your real accounts is a bigger trust leap than reviewing each step yourself. Its error recovery is only as good as the apps it's connected to — worth testing on something low-stakes before handing it anything sensitive.

Save this so you don't lose it, and try it on one small, annoying task this week. Full breakdown — link in bio.

slides.heading: You know the old way.
slides.body: Wire a trigger to an action, test it, watch it break on step three, then dig through logs to find out why.

slides.heading: Just type what you want to happen.
slides.body: No visual builder, no clicking steps together — describe the outcome in plain English and the agent constructs the whole multi-step workflow itself.

slides.heading: It doesn't just do one thing — it decides.
slides.body: The agent can branch into different paths depending on what it finds, instead of one rigid trigger-to-action chain that only works one way.

slides.heading: When something breaks, it doesn't just quietly die.
slides.body: It retries or reroutes instead of failing silently — though it's only as reliable as the apps it's connected to. Start it on low-stakes tasks first.

slides.heading: It already speaks to everything you use.
slides.body: Email, calendar, spreadsheets, your CRM, social accounts — the agent taps into Zapier's 7,000+ existing integrations instead of starting from zero.

slides.heading: This isn't just an office tool.
slides.body: Log a package tracking email into your notes, text yourself restock alerts, or fold every starred newsletter into one weekly digest — automatically.

slides.heading: The fiddly babysitting part disappears.
slides.body: What used to be trigger, test, fix, retest, and periodic checking becomes one sentence — and the agent handles the rest, including the parts that used to break.

slides.heading: Automation you describe, not one you build.
slides.body: Zapier's AI Agents write, run, and maintain multi-step workflows from a plain-English prompt — reaching general availability in July 2026.
